chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Dawood Bin Razeyn, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who remembers his difficulty (bereavement), and even though it may be after a while,
Surely we are for Allah and to Him we are returning
and the praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds
O Allah! Recompense me upon my difficulty and Replace upon me that which is superior than it,
would have for him from the Recompense, similar to what he had during the first shock.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Baqarah 2:156 after a delay following a bereavement?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of reward for mourning, affirming that delayed recitation of the verse of return and specific supplications yields the same merit as immediate response. It underscores the theological principle that sincere remembrance of loss, regardless of timing, maintains the spiritual connection to divine mercy and compensation. This teaching encourages believers to engage in active mourning practices rather than passive resignation, reinforcing the value of verbalized gratitude and petition in times of grief.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Dawood Bin Razeyn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who remembers his difficulty (bereavement), and even though it may be after a while,
so he says [2:156] Surely we are for Allah and to Him we are returning
and [1:2] The praise is due to Allah, the Lord of the Worlds
. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Recompense me upon my difficulty and Replace upon me that which is superior than it’,
would have for him from the Recompense, similar to what he had during the first shock’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Dawud ibn Razin who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
if one recalls his suffering a misfortune
even after a long time and says, ‘To Allah we belong and to Him we return,
all praise belongs to Allah Lord of the worlds;
O Lord, grant me favors for my suffering a misfortune and replace my losses with something better,’
his reward for this is equal to that he deserved upon suffering it the first time.”
